name: CT-996

lead: CT-996 (tifeglipron) is an experimental oral GLP-1 agonist from Roche for obesity and type 2 diabetes. Fat-loss communities follow it as a non-injectable alternative to semaglutide-type drugs, with lower appetite leading to weight loss and a leaner body.

It is a small molecule taken by mouth, rather than a peptide injection, and small-molecule oral GLP-1 drugs are designed to avoid the injection requirement. Evidence so far consists of clinical trial registrations covering phase 1 and phase 2 studies; published results were not found.

paras: It is not available outside trials. In development it is a pill for people with obesity or type 2 diabetes.
No published safety data were found, and it is not approved.

web.title: CT-996 phase 1 weight loss results - Pharmaceutical Executive

angle.text: CT-996 is an experimental oral GLP-1 pill that activates the same appetite pathway as semaglutide-type drugs, lowering appetite for weight loss and a leaner body without injections. It has registered phase 2 trials and no published results yet.

lead: CT-996 is an investigational oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist from Roche, also registered under the code RO7795081 and the name tifeglipron [1][2]. It is being developed as a once-daily pill for weight loss and for type 2 diabetes, so its appearance relevance is fat loss: people interested in a leaner body and face follow GLP-1 drugs such as semaglutide, and an oral option is a topic of interest in that community.

Small-molecule oral GLP-1 agonists are a class designed to avoid the injection requirement of peptide drugs; a 2025 review describes them as acting at non-canonical sites in the receptor with biased G-protein signalling [3]. CT-996 came to Roche through its acquisition of Carmot Therapeutics, announced on 4 December 2023 for USD 2.7 billion in cash plus up to USD 400 million in milestones, which then described CT-996 as a once-daily oral agent in phase 1 [4].

Roche reported topline phase 1 results in July 2024, describing a placebo-adjusted mean weight loss of 6.1% within four weeks in participants with obesity but without type 2 diabetes [5]. Phase 2 studies in obesity and type 2 diabetes have since been registered [2][6]. It is not approved anywhere and is not available outside trials.

paras: A review of small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonists says these nonpeptidic agents act mainly through non-canonical orthosteric sites within the receptor transmembrane domain, producing G-protein-biased signalling with reduced beta-arrestin-mediated adverse effects, and notes that orforglipron has advanced furthest in the class [3]. Peptide GLP-1 drugs are injected; a pill avoids that route [3].

Roche's phase 1 announcement, as reported by trade press, described CT-996 as a biased agonist that activates cAMP signalling with minimal beta-arrestin recruitment, and said blood levels were little affected whether participants were fasting or had eaten a high-fat meal, suggesting it could be taken regardless of meal timing [5].

Roche announced a definitive agreement to acquire Carmot Therapeutics on 4 December 2023 for USD 2.7 billion in cash at closing plus up to USD 400 million in milestone payments. The assets included CT-996, an oral once-daily GLP-1 receptor agonist in phase 1 for obesity with or without type 2 diabetes, CT-388, a once-weekly subcutaneous dual GLP-1/GIP agonist, and CT-868, a daily dual agonist for type 1 diabetes with overweight [4]. Registrations since then use the code RO7795081 and the name tifeglipron [2].

The phase 1 study (CT-996-201) was double-blind and placebo-controlled. Part 1 enrolled 40 overweight or obese participants on single ascending doses; part 2 enrolled three sequential cohorts of 25 participants with obesity but without type 2 diabetes on multiple ascending doses [5]. Roche reported a placebo-adjusted mean weight loss of 6.1% within four weeks, mostly mild or moderate gastrointestinal adverse events, and no discontinuations due to adverse events [5]. Roche's chief medical officer Levi Garraway said the company was pleased to see clinically meaningful weight loss [5]. A third part in 30-person cohorts with type 2 diabetes was planned [5]. Analyst commentary reported in news coverage noted the early time point and small sample size, so the figure comes from a short, small study.

A completed phase 1 study in overweight or obese participants and people with type 2 diabetes enrolled 94 people from May 2023 [1]. A phase 2 study of daily oral tifeglipron in 352 people with obesity or overweight and at least one weight-related comorbidity began in July 2025 and is listed as completed [2]. A 330-person phase 2 study from August 2025 compares different doses with placebo or semaglutide in type 2 diabetes [6].

Further phase 1 studies registered include a drug-interaction study of approved medications in 36 healthy participants (2025) [7], a multiple-dose study in 30 Chinese adults with overweight or obesity (2026) [8], a statin interaction study in 40 people (2025) [9], and a renal impairment study of 60 participants (2026) [10]. No results have been published.

CT-996 is one of several oral GLP-1 candidates under development alongside orforglipron [3]. Roche has said it hopes CT-996 could support glycemic control and weight loss and possibly serve as maintenance therapy after weight loss with injectable drugs [5]. It is not available outside clinical trials.

timeline.event: Phase 1 study of CT-996 begins (May) [1]; Roche announces acquisition of Carmot Therapeutics (December) [4].
Roche reports positive phase 1 results, 6.1% placebo-adjusted weight loss at four weeks (July) [5].
Phase 2 studies of tifeglipron start in obesity and type 2 diabetes [2][6].
